brief.prose: The station is laid out as a curve. The visiting berths and the pressure lobby are at one end; the Republic Customs Hall is the first room every arrival stands in; the Yard Concourse is the spine, and every public desk opens off it: the harbourmaster, the Materials Exchange (with its public rung stair down to Kasei's receiving counter on the Freight Deck), the commissary, the Stickney service counter, the Shift Board mess and the observation gallery over the drydocks. Twelve rooms carry the slice; the pasted P06 Bonded Freight Hall, P13 Freight Transfer Junction and P14 Tank Service Gallery are reconciled out as §0.3 says (their only loop purpose arrives with the freight-deck cut P-F) and stay visible as background through the receiving office's barred window and the gallery's ports. One restricted room, the Yard Maintenance Spine, is staff-locked and hidden off the receiving office on the staff-lobby precedent; it holds the storefront items that back the counters and the dark desks where doc 11's principals sit enabled:false until the faction cut binds them.

ambience: The shift bell sounds twice, and the handline traffic on the concourse reverses direction.
A pressure door cycles somewhere toward the berths; the counter above it clicks over.
Pump vibration from the refinery rises through the deck, holds, and settles back into the boot-cleats.
A work lamp on the crater floor goes out, and a moment later another comes on two cradles over.
The approach-control channel mutters a cutter's callsign and a bearing, then returns to static.
Frost from the refinery stacks falls back across the pad in a slow white curtain.
Someone pins a new card to the Shift Board wall and takes an older one down without reading it.
The commissary's cold-locker drips into its tray, once, and the hum changes pitch.
A dolly alarm chirps in the bonded hall and stops.
Mars has turned by a degree that nobody noticed, and the terminator has moved onto Coprates.
A Guard recruiting bill loses a corner to the ventilation and curls a little further.
The berth board updates: one cradle goes from IDLE to CLEARED, and the room's attention goes with it.
def.name: Stickney Yards

theme.name: TacSim 2350: the Yards
theme.style_guide: Present tense, no second person, no named NPCs in a room desc. Each room is distinct in sound, light and smell before it is distinct in furniture. Phobos holds nothing down (doc 10 §3: no artificial gravity beyond thrust and rotation): decks are painted conventions, handlines run everywhere, benches have tether loops, and "down" is where the arrows point. The Republic sounds institutional (doc 11 framing: governments institutional, corporations brands): forms in triplicate, posted charges initialled, crests, shift boards instead of advertising. Kasei and the Yard sound like brands: stencils, price cards, RESERVED. Power shows as paperwork and as who may walk through which door. Mars is in the sky and the refinery is in the floor. Desc length medium (60–120 words); details are one or two sentences, dry, with a fact in them. Exit aliases avoid the kernel words.

def.desc: The gallery runs the length of the visiting berths behind a wall of thick ports, each framing a cradle, a boarding tube and the stencilled number of the berth beyond. Handlines are strung the full length at shoulder height; Phobos holds nothing down, and the deck is a convention painted in yellow arrows. The air carries the cold-metal tang of a lock that has just cycled and a faint ozone of welders somewhere out in the crater. A berth board lists what sits in each cradle, who it answers to and what it owes. The pressure lobby is inward, and everything else is through the lobby.

details.berth board: Cradle by cradle: the hull, its registry, its agent of record, CLEARED or HELD. A docked hull's name lights when a pilot is aboard.
details.boarding tubes: Each tube ends at a lock plate and a cycle counter. The tubes are the station's: a ship's own lock is on the other side of the counter.
details.handlines: Braided line at shoulder height, clip points every two metres. The convention is right-hand traffic; the sign says so in Coprates typeface.
details.ports: Thick laminated glass with a Republic inspection sticker in each corner, dated. Beyond them the boarding tubes, and past those the crater floor's work lamps.

def.name: Visiting Berth Gallery
def.short_desc: A long pressurised gallery along the visiting berths, handlines strung the length of it.

def.desc: A square chamber between two pressure doors, each a hand-span of Stickney alloy with a Republic inspection sticker on its frame and a cycle counter glowing above it. There is no side exit and nothing to buy; the room exists so that nobody is ever one door from vacuum. Tether clips hang from a rail by the inner door, and a wall placard in Republic typeface lists the order of operations if the gallery door fails to seal. The air is still, a little over-pressured, and smells of door grease. The berth gallery is outward; the customs hall is inward.

details.cycle counter: Six digits over each door. The gallery side is higher by a hundred thousand; ships come and go more than people do.
details.inspection sticker: Orbital Guard Harbour Safety, a date, a stamp, a signature that is only a line.
details.placard: IN THE EVENT OF SEAL FAILURE: 1. Do not open the inner door. 2. Clip on. 3. Wait. Initialled by three inspectors, the last one this month.

def.name: Pressure Lobby
def.short_desc: A square chamber between two pressure doors and nothing else.

def.desc: Queue rails in brushed alloy divide the hall into numbered lanes that end at a counter with a slot for forms and a scanner for manifests. The Republic's crest is set into the far wall over a board of posted charges, every line of it initialled. Form racks stand by the door — Entry Declaration, Manifest Attestation, Crew Roster — in triplicate pads with the carbons still in. The light is flat and white and the ventilation loud; the hall smells of toner and of coffee gone cold on a hotplate. The pressure lobby is outward; the yard concourse is through the far doors.

details.crest: The Assembly's crest in cast alloy, Stickney-made, with the Settlement year under it.
details.forms: Three pads, Republic typeface, triplicate. The Crew Roster asks for every manifested person and the hull's agent of record; the Entry Declaration asks what the hold carries and who signed for it at origin.
details.posted charges: Berthing, by the IC day. Manifest attestation, per hull. Inspection, at the Guard's discretion. Every figure initialled; the column for Belt-flagged hulls has been re-stuck twice.
details.scanner: A manifest reader bolted to the counter. It reads; a petty officer decides. The placard under it says so, in the Warrant's own words.

def.name: Republic Customs Hall
def.short_desc: A low hall of numbered queue rails under a Republic crest.

def.desc: A wide corridor curves with the crater wall, its outer face studded with viewports and its inner face given over to shift boards: crew call lists, drydock rotations, a Guard recruiting bill with its corners curling. There is no advertising. Handlines run both ways down the middle and traffic keeps right by habit. Pump vibration from the refinery comes up through the deck, a hum felt in the boot-cleats before it is heard. The air is warm and tastes of alloy dust. Doors open off the concourse to the harbourmaster, the materials exchange, the commissary, the service counter, the Shift Board mess and the observation gallery; the customs hall is back toward the locks.

details.handlines: Two lines, inbound and outbound, with a painted arrow every five metres. Newcomers hold both.
details.recruiting bill: ORBITAL GUARD — THE CORRIDOR IS OURS TO KEEP. A Vigil at full torch, drawn larger than it is. Someone has pencilled a tally under it.
details.shift boards: Drydock 2 on third rotation; Drydock 4 RESERVED — GUARD; a crew call for a Hod refit, Settlement citizens preferred. A public map of the station hangs at the end, the Freight Deck drawn as a grey band marked YARD PERSONNEL.
details.viewports: Small, round, thick. Through each one a slice of crater floor, a truss, a work lamp, and a scrap of Mars.

def.name: Yard Concourse
def.short_desc: The yard's one wide corridor, shift boards down both walls.

def.desc: A half-door with a counter on top of it closes off a narrow office papered in berth assignments. On the back wall a board shows every cradle in the visiting berths — occupied, cleared, overdue — and under it two clocks, one in Freeport time and one in Coprates standard, disagreeing by the margin two governments can keep up over a calendar. Clearance stamps sit in a tray; a sailing-plan pad lies open to today's page. A radio mutters the Guard's approach-control channel at a volume that is just not words. The office smells of stamp ink and strong tea. The concourse is out the half-door.

details.berth board: Cradle, hull, CLEARED or OVERDUE, and the hour of the next filed departure. A hull with no sailing plan is listed as IDLE, in a colour meant to shame.
details.clocks: Freeport time on the left, Coprates standard on the right. A card between them gives the offset, in case anyone asks why the Belt's day and the Republic's disagree; the clerk has an opinion about which is right.
details.radio: Approach control, the Guard's voice, a cutter's callsign, a bearing. Then static, which is most of it.
details.sailing plan pad: Departure at, destination, manifest sealed Y/N, sell at destination, agent of record, SIGNED. A plan can be filed days ahead and amended until the burn; after it, the pad says SAILED and nothing else, and the harbourmaster's office runs its lines under the captain's signature whether the captain is awake or not.

def.name: Harbourmaster's Office
def.short_desc: A narrow office behind a half-door, the berth board glowing on the back wall.

def.desc: The receiving office stands at the boundary between paperwork and freight: a scarred counter with a manifest scanner and a set of assay scales, and behind it a barred window onto the bonded hall, where pallets move on tracked dollies under yellow light. A board over the counter states Kasei's remaining intake for the cycle and what it pays, line by line. Warehouse air blows through — colder, drier, sharp with hydraulic fluid — and somewhere beyond the bars a dolly alarm chirps and stops. The exchange is up the stair; a hatch in the back wall is stencilled YARD PERSONNEL.

details.assay scales: A bench of grade scales and a core sampler. A lot's grade is read here and written on the manifest; the price is per tonne of what the scales say, not what the seller says.
details.barred window: The bonded hall: racked pallets under yellow lamps, tracked dollies, a manifest clerk on a tether, and a freight door at the far end with a berth number beside it. No public way in.
details.hatch: An alloy hatch with a card reader and no handle on this side. YARD PERSONNEL ONLY, and under it, smaller, THAT MEANS YOU.
details.intake board: CONCENTRATE — the bid, per tonne — intake remaining. WATER ICE — the bid, per tonne — intake remaining; the figures are the board's own and change when Kasei says so. The concentrate line has been painted over once, downward; the refinery is water-starved and bids the ice up and the ore down, and the clerk will say so if asked. FUNDS: a figure Kasei does not hide, because it is the figure that decides whether a hull gets paid today.

def.name: Kasei Receiving Office
def.short_desc: A counter on the warehouse side, an assay bench behind it, the bonded hall through a barred window.

def.desc: Kasei's prices fill one wall: structural alloy stock by the tonne, drive propellant by the tonne, each line with a quantity beside it that goes down and never, in anyone's memory here, up. The opposite wall is bids, mostly Kasei's own for metal concentrate and water ice, a few private lines from yard contractors in smaller type. Between the walls the floor is bare alloy scored by pallet feet, and a rung stair in a railed well goes down to the receiving counter. The room is cold — warehouse air leaks up the well — and smells of machine oil. The concourse is out; receiving is down the stair.

details.bids board: KASEI METALS BUYS: concentrate and water ice, the bid per tonne beside each line with the intake left this cycle; the figures are the board's own, never the paint's. Under it, contractors' chits: a tonne of alloy offcuts wanted, a Hod seat to Isidis offered.
details.floor: Pallet scoring in the alloy, in parallel lines from the well to the door. Freight used to come up this way. Now it does not, and the lines are a record.
details.price board: ALLOY STOCK, STRUCTURAL — per t — remaining. PROPELLANT, DRIVE — per t — remaining. The figures are Kasei's and change when Kasei says so. Below Kasei's lines, in the Yard's own stencil: YARD FITTINGS, CRATED — PER TONNE, THE YARD'S FIGURE — STICKNEY YARDS — SIGNED AT THE SERVICE COUNTER, with a chalked note beside it, CRATED: 2.3 CUBES TO THE TONNE. A Dray captain who reads both boards sees the return run's arithmetic: alloy stock fills the rating, fittings fill the bay, and the hull that leaves with both full pays best.
details.stair well: A rung stair in a railed well, seven metres down to the Freight Deck, with a handline beside the rungs for those who prefer to float it. RECEIVING COUNTER — PUBLIC; the arrow is green.

def.name: Materials Exchange
def.short_desc: A trading floor the size of a cargo bay, asks on one wall and bids on the other.

def.desc: Shelving in alloy racks runs back from a counter, crates of voyage provisions stacked by the crew-day, and the Republic's posted price stencilled on a board beside the till — one figure, no haggling line. A cold-locker hums at the back and drips into a tray. The counter has a cage over it that is only half closed, and a hand-lettered sign gives the hours, which are the shift bells. The room smells of cardboard and the sweet tang of ration bars and is the warmest on the deck. The concourse is out.

details.crates: Sealed crew-day crates, four kilos a day: food, potable stores, scrubber cartridges. A crate opened on a shelf shows what a day looks like. It does not look like much.
details.price posting: VOYAGE PROVISIONS — per crew-day — posted by the Assembly's Office of Supply. The figure has a date. There is no second figure.
details.sign: OPEN FIRST BELL TO LAST BELL. CLOSED FOR INVENTORY WHEN THE DOOR IS SHUT. Both in the same hand.

def.name: Yard Commissary
def.short_desc: A stores counter under a Republic posting, shelves of ration crates behind.

def.desc: Long tables bolted to the deck, benches with tether loops under them, and a serving hatch with a chalk menu that has not changed in a year. After the shift bell the hatch turns into a bar. The walls are the station's unofficial notice board — crew wanted, a bunk for rent, a Dray's worth of alloy offcuts going cheap, a card for a dockworkers' meeting that nobody has taken down. A Settlement-era photograph of the yard strike hangs over the hatch. The room is loud and warm and smells of fried protein and coffee that has been on the heater since the last shift. The concourse is out.

details.chalk menu: Protein, fried. Protein, not fried. Soup (ask). Coffee. After the bell the word BEER appears under it in a different chalk.
details.hatch: A serving hatch with a heat lamp over it and a tally sheet beside it for crews who settle on payday.
details.notice wall: CREW WANTED, DRAY, CERES RUN, SHARE BASIS. BUNK TO LET, QUIET, NO GUARD. And a plain card, no name: DOCKWORKERS — THURSDAY — THE USUAL PLACE.
details.photograph: The Phobos yard strike, 2309: a drydock floor full of people on tethers, holding a banner that reads OUR YARD. One young face at the front is circled in pencil, and someone has written the word YARDMASTER beside it with no comment.

def.name: The Shift Board
def.short_desc: A mess hall that doubles as a bar after the shift bell.

def.desc: A counter of worn alloy under the Yard's stencil, with a card rack of every hull class Stickney builds — Vigil, Hod, Anvil, Cairn, Dray — and a price card for a new Dray clipped to the front of it. A window behind the counter frames a drydock cradle with a hull in it and a work crew on tethers under a lamp. A board lists yard-time by the drydock-day, most lines marked RESERVED. Nothing here promises a repair; the board says ENQUIRE. A second, smaller sign on the counter's end carries a Luna insurer's mark. The room smells of solvent from the shop beyond the wall. The concourse is out.

details.Dray price card: DRAY-CLASS BULK HAULER, NEW, STICKNEY BUILD — 120,000cr, delivery subject to yard-time. The card is the figure a charter pilot measures a career against. Under it, in pencil: "used ones exist, ask Tycho".
details.fittings card: YARD FITTINGS, CRATED — PER TONNE — REMAINING — pressure fittings, ducting and tank sections, Stickney build, crated with dunnage for the Belt run. In pen under it: "2.3 cubes to the tonne. Your problem, captain." The Yard's one line of trade, signed by the clerk; the figures under it are the Yard's own and change when the Yard says so.
details.hull cards: A card per class with a profile drawing and a dry mass. The Dray's reads "slow, efficient, unarmed"; the Vigil's reads "fast, expensive, visible from a long way off", which is the Yard quoting the Guard's own brochure.
details.insurers mark: TYCHO MUTUAL ASSURANCE & SALVAGE — AGENT IN ATTENDANCE. Renewals, claims, the Re-float Program by referral to Kirkwood. The agent shares the counter and the clerk's patience.
details.window: A cradle, a hull with its drive section open, three workers on tethers and one supervisor who is not. The work is slow. It is always slow, and it is always going on.
details.yard time board: Drydock-days by cradle. RESERVED — GUARD. RESERVED — KASEI. One line reads ENQUIRE and that is the refit queue; no date is promised on it.

def.name: Stickney Service Counter
def.short_desc: A yard counter with a rack of hull cards and a window onto a drydock.

def.desc: The gallery is a curve of floor-to-ceiling ports along the crater's rim. Below, the drydock trusses stand in rows across the crater floor, cradles lit by work lamps, and beyond them the Guard's pad with two cutters berthed nose-out and a third cradle empty. Past the pad the refinery's stacks vent in slow white plumes that fall back as frost. Above, Mars fills a quarter of the sky, rust and white, turning so slowly it seems not to. The gallery is kept dim so the view reads; the only sound is the air plant and the tick of the ports cooling. It smells of nothing, which on Phobos is a luxury. Benches with tether loops face the glass. The concourse is out.

details.Guard pad: Two Vigil-class cutters, torch nozzles capped, berthed nose-out toward the lane. A cutter leaves the pad maybe once a week, and the whole crater watches it go.
details.Mars: A quarter of the sky, Coprates somewhere under the dust, the terminator a soft line. Phobos keeps one face to it, so it never sets.
details.drydocks: Six cradles in two rows on the crater floor, trusses taller than the rim walk. Three hold hulls; one holds a Dray with its hold open like a jaw. The Yard builds for the Republic and "for a price, for anyone the Republic licenses".
details.refinery: Kasei's stacks beyond the pad, venting. Water ice goes in at one end; propellant and alloy stock come out the other, and the Freeport's bank holds the paper on the whole of it.

def.name: Yard Observation Gallery
def.short_desc: A dim curved gallery of windows over Stickney crater.

def.desc: A service corridor runs behind the freight deck, cable trays overhead, pump manifolds along one wall, and three wire cages holding the manifolds and lockers that feed the counters above: Kasei's intake and store, the commissary's provisions, the Yard's spares. At the far end a glassed office looks down into the bonded hall — three desks, three dark terminals, nameplates face down. The air is cold and loud with pumps and smells of hydraulic fluid. YARD PERSONNEL ONLY is stencilled every ten metres. The receiving hatch is the way out.

details.cages: KASEI — INTAKE & STORE. COMMISSARY — PROVISIONS. YARD — SPARES. Each cage has a manifest clipped to it, and the manifests are the station's real stock, not the boards upstairs.
details.manifolds: Propellant from the refinery, water from the bunker, air from the plant, each valve tagged with a date and an initial.
details.office: Three desks: the managing director's, the yardmaster's, and one with a Guard crest, kept for a commodore who prefers the pad. The terminals are dark. The nameplates are face down on purpose.

def.name: Yard Maintenance Spine
def.short_desc: A service corridor of cable trays and storefront cages, the yard office glassed off at its end.

def.truth: Commodore Bask "believes one seized hauler ends the argument" (§3.2). The empty third cradle on the Guard's pad is kept empty for a reason, and the Customs Assertion clock advances on "each successful interdiction at Kirkwood" (§6). A Freeport-flagged Dray is the hauler he means.

the Office of Territorial Security "wants a tap" on the Phobos relay half; "whether it has one is a seed-pack secret" (doc 15 §4). OTS is also "trying to buy" the Tether (§4.6). The Thursday card on the Shift Board's wall is watched by someone who is not a dockworker.
